READING

**The numbers as given**

Both courses carry the same GBP 27,072 of learning-curve remakes because ten technicians must cross regardless. That cost cancels out of the comparison. What differs is:

| Item | AVENSWOOD | KIRKBANE |
|---|---|---|
| Overtime spend | GBP 0 | GBP 44,000 |
| Crossing remakes | Elevated over 9 months | Near zero |
| Peak lab remake rate | ~5–6% | ~10% |
| Practices seeing peak simultaneously | A fraction | All 40 |

---

**Effective remake rate during the transition**

*KIRKBANE, January 2027.*
Ten technicians move together. By January 2027 the pilot pair has been on the new system for about eight months (~430 units each), putting them somewhere between the 300-unit rate (4.2%) and the 900-unit rate (3.4%) — call it roughly 4.1%. The ten new arrivals are at 11.4%.

Lab-wide effective rate:
- 10 technicians on new system: (10/12) × 31 × 11.4 % ≈ 2.95 remakes/day
- 2 pilot technicians: (2/12) × 31 × 4.1 % ≈ 0.21 remakes/day
- Total: ~3.16 remakes against 31 units shipped — **≈10.2%**

That is more than three times the settled rate of 3.1%, and every one of the forty practices sees it in the same month. A practice that sends twelve units and gets one back in January will send ten in February. It is not obvious that the relationship recovers just because the rate is back to normal by autumn.

*AVENSWOOD, wave 1 worst case (January 2027).*
Three technicians on new system at 11.4%, two pilot technicians at ~4.1%, seven technicians on Kessendale at 3.1%:
- 3 new: (3/12) × 31 × 11.4 % ≈ 0.88 remakes/day
- 2 pilot: (2/12) × 31 × 4.1 % ≈ 0.21 remakes/day
- 7 settled: (7/12) × 31 × 3.1 % ≈ 0.56 remakes/day
- Total: ~1.65 remakes against 31 — **≈5.3%**

That is a noticeable uptick but not a crisis. The practices that tend to receive work from the three technicians in wave 1 will notice; those whose work runs through the other nine will see nothing unusual. No single practice is likely to form the impression that the laboratory has lost its grip.

---

**Crossing remakes under AVENSWOOD**

The pilot logged 40 crossing remakes in four months with the lab running two systems side by side. AVENSWOOD runs two systems for nine months. If crossing-remake frequency scales roughly with the duration of the dual-system period (the conservative assumption), that implies around 90 additional remakes — GBP 8,640. Even doubling that estimate for the larger number of technicians cycling through the mixed environment, the figure stays well below GBP 44,000. The crossing remake risk under AVENSWOOD does not come close to eroding the overtime saving.

The more important question is whether a nine-month dual-library period creates practice-facing errors — incorrect shade communication, a technician matching against the wrong reference. The problem statement notes the practices work from the lab's shade notes rather than maintaining their own. Managing two libraries is operationally real, but it is a defined administrative task, not an open-ended quality risk, and it resolves on 2027-10-04 when the last technician moves.

---

**Deadline compliance**

Under AVENSWOOD the last technician moves to the new system on 2027-10-04, leaving eight months and twenty-six days before Kessendale loses support on 2028-06-30. Kessendale is fully decommissioned well inside the window.

Under KIRKBANE all ten move on 2027-01-04, which is earlier and also inside the window. The deadline does not discriminate between the two courses.

---

**Peer support and learning**

AVENSWOOD moves three technicians at a time. Three people working through the same learning curve together can compare outputs, flag early anomalies, and calibrate against one another — the same dynamic that presumably helped the pilot pair. KIRKBANE puts ten people on the steep part simultaneously. While it is true that collective training resources can be concentrated, ten individuals all struggling with 11.4% remake rates is harder to manage than three, and there is no stable experienced bench to absorb overflow or provide informal reference.

---

**Summary**

KIRKBANE spends GBP 44,000 of real cash, buys a brief simplification in shade-library management, and imposes a 10%-plus remake rate on forty practices in the same calendar month. AVENSWOOD costs GBP 44,000 less in cash, carries a manageable crossing-remake liability estimated at GBP 8,000–20,000, keeps the peak remake rate below 6%, and distributes any quality impact across practices and time so that no single relationship is put under stress. Both courses clear the 2028-06-30 deadline with room to spare. AVENSWOOD is the stronger choice.

---

READING
AVENSWOOD protects practice relationships by keeping the peak lab-wide remake rate around 5% rather than over 10%, avoids the certain GBP 44,000 overtime outlay, and clears the 2028-06-30 deadline comfortably; the nine-month dual-system period and its crossing-remake exposure do not come close to offsetting those advantages.

CALL
AVENSWOOD

GROUNDS
Staggering the moves holds the worst-case remake rate to roughly half what a simultaneous move produces, shields all forty practice relationships from a lab-wide quality shock, and saves a certain GBP 44,000 in overtime at a crossing-remake cost that cannot plausibly exceed it.
